name: template-language
body:
Template language: layouts (`layout.html.tmpl`) are standard Go html/template; the only functions available are the documented v1 set.
- Content arrives pre-rendered: the body, `text` fields (inline Markdown) and each named section are passed as safe HTML. Other fields are passed as typed values: number/date already formatted per their `_format`, boolean, enum, list, image/link URLs.
- Sections render bottom-up: each section instance is executed through its own `layout.html.tmpl`, deepest first, and each parent receives every child section as a list of trusted HTML, one element per child instance (e.g. `{{ range .blocks }}{{ . }}{{ end }}`). This holds at every depth and for top-level slide sections too: section instances arrive at a slide layout as rendered HTML, not as data maps. A section template used as a field type remains data-only nesting — typed YAML values, never HTML.
- Markdown is rendered before layouts run: layouts receive pre-rendered HTML and do not parse Markdown themselves (there is no markdown helper).
- The custom function set is minimal and centrally defined and documented. v1 has exactly one helper: `media "path"`, whose argument is a path relative to `templates/media/` only (e.g. `{{media "logo.svg"}}` → `templates/media/logo.svg`), returning that file's served URL. The argument is a relative path that stays within `templates/media/`; a missing file, an absolute path or a `..` segment is a templates error qualified with the layout's file:line (requirements.constraint.media-paths-library-relative). The `media` helper resolves only within the library's `media/` tree — never into `themes/`: theme-owned files (fonts, logos in `themes/<name>/`) are referenced from a theme's CSS and are served from the theme directory. A theme's `theme.css` — and every CSS it `@import`s, wherever that CSS lives — may reference the library's shared `media/` tree and another theme's files using the reserved `media:` and `theme:<name>/` URL prefixes, for both `url()` and `@import`, validated the same way and rewritten to the served URL (theme-media-references); these are theme-CSS reference forms, not layout helpers — the v1 helper set stays exactly `media`. Adding a helper is a spec change.
- Every layout and every section template, at any depth, is additionally executed with a reserved deck/slide/item data context (see template-context, item-context): `deck` carries the deck-wide `title`, `author`, `date` and the author's `properties`; `slide` carries the derived position label `number` (a string: the slide's number, plus its letter for a vertical slide) and the integer `total`; `item` carries the current instance's place among its siblings (`index`, `number`, `count`, `first`, `last`, `section`, `template` and `parent`), nil/absent at slide level. This context is data carried alongside the field values, not a helper — the v1 function set stays exactly `media` — and `deck`/`slide`/`item` are reserved top-level names (requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names).
- Layouts render from the supplied data alone, with no file, environment or network access.
- Layout parse and execute errors are file:line-qualified templates errors (parse at templates-dir-validation step 3; `media` arguments checked at step 6; execute errors during example/deck render reported as templates errors).
AC: a layout using any function other than the documented set fails to parse with a file:line templates error; a layout referencing `{{media "logo.svg"}}` with `templates/media/logo.svg` present renders its served URL; `{{media "missing.svg"}}`, `{{media "../x"}}` and `{{media "/abs"}}` each yield a templates error naming the layout file:line; body/text/section values render unescaped as HTML while other string values are auto-escaped; a layout or section template can read `{{.deck.title}}`, a property via `{{index .deck.properties "<key>"}}`, the string `{{.slide.number}}`/integer `{{.slide.total}}`, and the `{{.item.*}}` sibling descriptor; each child section reaches its parent as trusted HTML, so a slide layout ranging over a section list emits rendered section markup rather than data maps.
